catalog_quote: In addition to lacking tone, Garo lacks anything like the contrastive, or nearly contrastive, word stress of English. ... The first generalization about stress is that when bisyllabic nouns without suffixes are pronounced in isolation, and in the least emphatic or least marked fashion, they have a mild stress on the second syllable. ... Stress is easiest to isolate in two syllable words, but the strongest stress also seems to fall on the final syllable in nouns of more than two syllables. ... noun suffixes often leave the stress in place, on the last syllable of the noun stem. ... other case suffixes such as the accusative -ko, the possessive -ni, and the instrumental -cha also tend to leave the stress, on the previous syllable.
